name: Bhasa
credit: No portrait of Bhasa is known; the page shows a monogram tile.
bio: Bhasa is one of the earliest named Sanskrit dramatists. His date is uncertain: Kalidasa praises him by name in the prologue to his own Malavikagnimitra, so he is placed before Kalidasa, and modern scholars have proposed dates from about the 2nd to the 4th century AD. Nothing reliable is known of his life.

In 1912 the Indian scholar T. Ganapati Sastri published, in the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series, a group of thirteen anonymous plays found in manuscripts in Kerala and ascribed them to Bhasa; whether he wrote them all has been debated ever since. The best known is Svapnavasavadatta (The Vision of Vasavadatta), here in the Sanskrit and in the 1930 English translation of A. C. Woolner and Lakshman Sarup.
